name: Jinnah Convention Centre
assumptions: Height is not published: wall 18.2 m and dome rise 11.8 m (top about 31 m) are fitted to photos, scaling from the 22 m arched face in the OSM footprint.
Dome is centred on the footprint: the dossier's satellite dome point sits about 10 m off, attributed to image lean because all photos show it concentric.
Dome diameter 65 m is the dossier value; the panel layout is a six-sector triangulated grid of ten rings, matching the photos' triangles but not counted panel by panel.
All eight arched faces get four arches and all corner piers one column of three diamond windows per half, seen on about five faces; the north and north-west sides were not photographed.
Arch glass takes the blue tone of the April 2026 photo; older photos show it darker.
Cladding colour is a photo estimate; it reads white in older photos and warm stone in 2026.
Porch height 8.1 m fitted to its 6.2 m bay width; 5 by 5 outer arches counted; inner ring of 3 arches a side and the open centre size are estimates.
Sunken court floor level is a guess at 1.2 m below ground.
Red canopy between the building and porch comes from the satellite image only; its 6 m height and posts are guesses.
West and south-west glazed annexes are read from the satellite image only; their two-step form, depth and heights are estimates.
Green awning follows one 2024 aerial photo; it may be temporary.
Facade lettering seen in one 2026 photo is left out because it could not be read.
Roof-top plant, flag masts and the 2026 banners are not modelled; a CDA upgrade reported in Sept 2026 may change the look.
